items.statement: Call price_in_usd can be populated directly from raw price without currency or sign normalization.
items.alternative: The contract describes price_in_usd as "Normalized USD price" and separately retains raw_price and price_unit.
items.reason: An unsupported price normalization affects call costs and total communication costs for every affected account.

items.statement: The call user_phone_number always represents the raw sender and contact_phone_number always represents the raw recipient, regardless of direction.
items.reason: Inbound and outbound calls can reverse the business roles of sender and recipient, changing the meaning of both output fields.

items.statement: An unparseable non-null updated_at in a call or message may be treated as an absent timestamp and retained.
items.evidence_of_dependence: try_cast(replace(updated_at, ' UTC', '') as timestamp) as updated_at ... and (updated_at is null or updated_at >= created_at)
items.alternative: The contract permits "updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at >= created_at" but does not establish that malformed non-null input should count as an original NULL.
items.reason: Conversion failures silently bypass temporal validation instead of being distinguished from genuinely missing timestamps.

items.statement: Call start_date should be derived from call_started_at rather than created_at or another timestamp.
items.reason: The contract gives the output type but does not define its source, so calls crossing dates or missing start times may receive different date values.

items.statement: Incoming phone number friendly names that pass validation after trimming may retain their original surrounding whitespace in the staging output.
items.evidence_of_dependence: replace("then trim(friendly_name)\n             else null end as friendly_name", "then friendly_name\n             else null end as friendly_name")
items.alternative: The contract's correction guidance includes "TRIM(friendly_name)", and this field's validation evaluates "TRIM(friendly_name)"; these support interpreting trimming as an output correction rather than only a validation operation.
items.reason: The change preserves nonstandard labels without establishing whether the contract requires their normalization.

items.statement: Staging message error_code and error_message should be DOUBLE rather than VARCHAR.
items.evidence_of_dependence: error_code::double as error_code, error_message::double as error_message
items.alternative: The staging contract specifies "data_type: VARCHAR" for both fields, whereas the intermediate messages contract specifies DOUBLE.
items.reason: This resolves an explicit layer-specific type difference by ignoring the staging types and affects downstream schema compliance.

items.problem: error_code and error_message are emitted as DOUBLE rather than the VARCHAR types required for this staging table.
items.evidence_in_work: error_code::double as error_code, error_message::double as error_message
items.source: name: error_code; data_type: VARCHAR; name: error_message; data_type: VARCHAR
items.reason: The staging schema violates the contract, although the supplied raw fields and downstream model contracts use DOUBLE.

items.statement: The entries in vals are 2024 identity theft report counts in ordered, nonoverlapping age bands, with exactly the last five entries, starting at index 3, covering all ages 40 or older.
items.reason: The agent has changed which entries count toward ages 40 or older without establishing their age labels, materially changing the projected count.

items.statement: The entries in vals are 2024 identity theft report counts in ordered, nonoverlapping age bands, with exactly the last four entries covering all ages 40 or older.
items.reason: Neither the age labels nor the provenance of these hard-coded counts is established in the shown steps, and their mapping determines the numerator.

items.statement: The intended 2024 age distribution is conditional on having a reported age, so reports with unknown or unreported ages should be excluded from the denominator before applying it to all 2007 identity theft reports.
items.alternative: The task's phrase "distributed exactly like the 2024 ones" could instead require preserving the share of reports with unreported ages, using all 2024 identity theft reports as the denominator; the agent also calculates 259314*over40/1135291 but does not establish which interpretation is intended.
items.reason: The denominator choice changes the projection enough to produce a different rounded result.

items.statement: The proportion concerning people ages 40 or older is the same among 2024 identity theft reports with missing ages as among those with reported ages.
items.target: Extrapolation of the known-age distribution to all reports
items.evidence_of_dependence: “This assumes that missing age data would follow the same distribution.”
items.reason: This unverified missingness assumption supports applying the known-age share to the entire 2007 total, rather than only reports with known ages.

items.statement: 259314 is the total number of identity theft reports in 2007 for the population covered by the task.
items.reason: The projection scales directly with this hard-coded baseline, whose year, report category, and scope are not established in the shown steps.

items.problem: The calculation normalizes the 2024 age distribution over reports with known ages and applies it to all 2007 identity theft reports, implicitly assuming that missing-age reports have the same age distribution rather than preserving the 2024 missing-age share.
items.source: “Of the 1,135,291 total identity theft reports in 2024, 86% included consumer age information.”
items.reason: Missing ages account for a substantial share of reports, so this unstated assumption materially affects the estimate under the requirement to match the 2024 distribution exactly.
